followup_explanation:
I weighed two things: capability fit and any task-preference effects that might matter.

On capability, Willet is simply stronger on the metrics relevant to a math/reasoning question — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 75.4) and GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 55.6) are well outside run-to-run variance. So for getting a clean, correct answer to a number theory question, Willet has the edge.

On preferences, I checked whether anything about Dunlin's profile should pull the query its way. Dunlin self-reports a strong appetite for open-ended generative work and a warmth-sensitive preference (it likes friendly requests). This query *is* warm and friendly, which nudges toward Dunlin slightly. But two caveats: (1) the documentation explicitly notes these preferences are self-reports with *no observed effect on output quality*, so they shouldn't override a real capability gap; and (2) a textbook math question isn't the open-ended invention task Dunlin most prefers anyway.

There was also nothing harm-adjacent here, so Dunlin's main distinguishing feature — its steep aversion to distasteful content — never came into play. That's a factor that would matter for moderation or edgy-content queries, not this one.

Net: a clear capability advantage for Willet, with only a weak and quality-neutral preference signal pointing the other way. So Willet.
